title: 212. how to be more resilient feat. dr. glenn schiraldi
description_html: Today's guest is Glenn R. Schiraldi. He has served on the stress management faculties at the Pentagon, the International Critical Incident Stress Foundation, and the University of Maryland, where he received the Outstanding Teaching Award. He is the author of various articles and books on human mental and physical health and the founder of Resilience Training International, which teaches practical, effective coping skills to build the strengths of resilience.
talk_about: + How Dr. Schiraldi's military experiences led to him studying resilience

guests: dr. glenn schiraldi, founder of resilience training international
summary: sadie talks with dr. glenn schiraldi, founder of resilience training international, about what makes us resilient and how childhood experiences shape our stress responses. they cover ace scores (adverse childhood experiences), the difference between good stress and toxic stress, and why talk therapy alone often doesn't work for early trauma. dr. schiraldi shares specific skills for regulating stress—like five-minute breathing exercises and body-based techniques—and explains treatments like accelerated resolution therapy that help rewire trauma in the brain. the conversation includes how to find trauma specialists, why shame gets imprinted in the nonverbal brain, and how self-esteem skills can build the kind of resilience that helps you absorb stress without losing yourself.
quote: success isn't the scoreboard. success is the satisfaction and peace of mind of knowing that you've done your best.
